==Problem==

How many 4-digit positive integers have four different digits, where the leading digit is not zero, the integer is a multiple of 5, and 5 is the largest digit?

<imath> \textbf{(A) }24\qquad\textbf{(B) }48\qquad\textbf{(C) }60\qquad\textbf{(D) }84\qquad\textbf{(E) }108 </imath>

===Sidenote===
This question expects you to actually HAVE a 5 in it.

==Solution 1==
We can separate this into two cases. If an integer is a multiple of <imath>5,</imath> the last digit must be either <imath>0</imath> or <imath>5.</imath>

Case 1: The last digit is <imath>5.</imath> The leading digit can be <imath>1,2,3,</imath> or <imath>4.</imath> Because the second digit can be <imath>0</imath> but not the leading digit, there are also <imath>4</imath> choices. The third digit cannot be the leading digit or the second digit, so there are <imath>3</imath> choices. The number of integers is this case is <imath>4\cdot4\cdot3\cdot1=48.</imath>

Case 2: The last digit is <imath>0.</imath> Because <imath>5</imath> is the largest digit, one of the remaining three digits must be <imath>5.</imath> There are <imath>3</imath> ways to choose which digit should be <imath>5.</imath> The remaining digits can be <imath>1,2,3,</imath> or <imath>4,</imath> but since they have to be different there are <imath>4\cdot3</imath> ways to choose. The number of integers in this case is <imath>1\cdot3\cdot4\cdot3=36.</imath>

Therefore, the answer is <imath>48+36=\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 84}</imath>.
